title: Test a two-handle faucet and file the fault report by ProffNdhlovu · Pull Request #1171 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: The diagnosis half of NSPIRE D161: the fixture is in one of three unannounced conditions (both handles work; a handle will not open; a handle will not shut off — the last two realized as a physical worn-stop post). The robot tests the handle by manipulation, then commits to a diagnosis by leaving the white report tag on the matching colored pad. Wrong-pad reports score 0.3, so guessing does not pay. Scripted demo reaches 1.0 in all three modes; Dream-1 baseline 0.0. Media M-ANEAP9.

Received as TK-4QAN67 , and waiting for review. The decision will be posted here: accepted tasks are merged, and tasks not accepted get feedback here, and you can push a revision to this pull request. Please don’t merge this pull request yourself.

Not accepted: final (TK-4QAN67). Flags: Egregious simplification · Scripted demo branches on hidden FAULT_MODE · The stated one-third expected score for random guessing ignores the 0.3 wrong-report credit; uniform guessing yields approximately 0.53. · The code uses separate x/y thresholds while the text describes a 2.5 cm centre-distance threshold. Importance (not met): Without water or a functioning valve, the task does not assess the claimed ability to diagnose failure to activate or shut off water. Construct validity (not met): The visible posts and tag-only score allow a correct or incorrect report to earn credit without testing either handle. Clarity and reproducibility (not met): The report pads are unlabelled in the scene and the instruction does not tell the robot which colour means which finding. Feasibility (not met): The scripted demo chooses its turning direction and report pad from the unannounced FAULT_MODE rather than robot-observable evidence. A housing inspection must determine whether water actually starts and stops; loose rotating blocks obstructed by external posts do not represent that skill. The tag-only score also rewards reports made without testing, and the demonstration chooses the answer from the hidden fault mode rather than observing the fixture. If you think this misjudges your task, reply on this pull request within 48 hours and a person will review it. This task doesn’t meet the importance bar, so it can’t be revised, and this pull request is now closed. You’re welcome to submit a different task in a new pull request.
